overview.body:
A plan for building [Manage releases](/features/release-management) and [Know what proves the app works](/features/end-to-end-test-catalog): the 45 accepted stories, in 59 Tasks over eight phases. Accepted records the intent, and nothing here is built yet.

## The shape of it

**One new record, and everything else extends what exists.** A release is a directory of small files under a new `___releases` root. The catalog is a view over existing test cases. The process overview is an ordinary whiteboard in a new role. Which tests a change affects is the walk `review test-plan` already does, freed from needing a review.

```text
___releases/
  template/
    template.json          # the versioning scheme
    steps/<id>.json        # one template step
  <id>.release/
    release.json           # version, range, milestone, released commit
    public.md              # public notes
    notes/<id>.json        # one internal note
    stories/<id>.json      # one story link, delivers or affects
    checklist/<id>.json    # one step: sentence, excerpts, code, ticked
___qa/
  suite.json               # where end-to-end tests live, a command template
```

As with Plans, a change rewrites the same small file and Git is the history, with no revisions or events. One file per note, step and link is what makes [releases merge cleanly](annotation:records); a list inside one file would conflict on almost every merge.

## Reading follows the established pattern

**Agents read all of this through `change-saga query`, the way they read every other record.** Plans and Tasks show what happens otherwise: an agent wanting a Task's essay has to extract it from the rendered viewer, because `query` has no operation for it. So [query comes in the same phase as the commands](annotation:query) rather than as a follow-up:

```sh
change-saga query releases --saga change.saga [--release ID|URN] [--milestone ID]
change-saga query release-template --saga change.saga
change-saga query release-status --saga change.saga --release ID
change-saga query e2e-catalog --saga change.saga [--test ID] [--feature ID] [--kind KIND]
change-saga query e2e-tests --saga change.saga --ref LOCATION
change-saga query e2e-tests --saga change.saga --against REV --head REV
```

These are one operation with an optional selector, as `query personas --persona` and `query quality --test` are, with no separate `show` command. They use the standard envelope, snapshot, pagination and errors, return text in full, and `query schema` describes them. `--ref`, `--against` and `--head` are flags query already has. The commands that write take `--json`, and `tests --format` is the only thing outside query, because a runner's command line is not JSON.

## The phases

Tasks within a phase can run in parallel, and a Task depends only on earlier phases.

1. **[Foundations](annotation:foundations).** Four independent pieces. An existing Saga must behave exactly as it does today, and [the first release record](annotation:foundations) proves it.
2. **[Records and the walk](annotation:records).** The small files, a derived catalog, and the walk learning the transitive flow: from a line to an Item, to its feature, to that feature's stories.
3. **Commands and queries.** [A release and its checklist](annotation:checklist), [notes and links](annotation:notes), and [reading through query](annotation:query).
4. **Workflows and derived facts.** [What lets an agent run a release](annotation:running), [what a release says and reaches](annotation:says), and [what the tests prove](annotation:tests).
5. **Sections and reports.** [The Releases side and the QA section](annotation:sections), then [one shared test answer and the remaining tools](annotation:sharing).
6. **[Reader pages](annotation:pages).** These render what earlier phases compute and hold no logic of their own.
7. **[Ticking, merging and documenting](annotation:ticking).** Browser ticks, merge tests in real Git, the format documentation, and setting this repository up.
8. **[A real release](annotation:real).** An agent runs this repository's next release, and what it trips over goes back into the guide.

## Decisions this builds on

- **Nothing blocks a release.** Marking one released lists what is open and proceeds. Commands refuse only a malformed record.
- **The tool answers and teams decide.** Every QA measure is informative and exits 0 whenever it can answer. An app with no end-to-end tests is fine.
- **The flow is transitive.** Connections come from walking the existing links, and each answer says what path it took. The same-file step departs from `review test-plan`'s rule against inferring from file proximity, so that command keeps its stricter behaviour unless asked with `--e2e`.
- **Results stay out of the Saga.** A proof step links to the run in CI, and no pass or fail is stored.

## What could change

The largest uncertainty is the walk: Phase 1 and 2's Tasks were sized from reading the code, and the review turned out to be used in few places, but its fixtures may find more. If time runs short, the stories marked `should` or `could` are the place to look. Three of them carry work the rest needs: declaring where tests live, the release page, and the proof step. The other eleven, such as promoting a step or listing thin spots, can be deferred with their Tasks without affecting anything else.

Plans and Tasks' own missing query operation is a separate piece of work outside this Plan.

title: Releases and the end-to-end test catalog
objective: Explain the work to be done and how it can be executed in parallel.
